title: English Practice Quiz 0951
description: A ten-question English practice quiz covering grammar, vocabulary and practical communication.

questions.question: Before a meeting begins, the organiser should share the ___.
questions.explanation: An agenda lists the topics planned for discussion.

questions.question: A person who leads a meeting is usually called the ___.
questions.explanation: The chairperson guides the meeting and manages discussion.

questions.question: If you want to speak during a formal meeting, you can say ___.
questions.explanation: This is a polite way to request a turn.

questions.question: The written record of decisions made at a meeting is called the ___.
questions.explanation: Minutes record important discussions, decisions and actions.

questions.question: An action item in meeting minutes should ideally include an owner and a ___.
questions.explanation: An owner and deadline make follow-up responsibilities clear.

questions.question: If a discussion moves away from the agenda, the chairperson may ___.
options: bring it back to the topic
questions.explanation: Returning to the agenda helps keep the meeting focused.

questions.question: A quorum is the minimum number of members needed to ___.
options: conduct official business at a meeting
questions.explanation: A quorum is the required minimum attendance for valid proceedings.

questions.question: To 'adjourn' a meeting means to ___.
questions.explanation: Adjourn means bring a meeting to an end or pause it.

questions.question: Which phrase politely asks a speaker to explain a point?
options: Could you clarify that point, please?
questions.explanation: A polite clarification request encourages understanding.

questions.question: A meeting follow-up email should summarise decisions and ___.
questions.explanation: Follow-up messages help participants remember agreed actions.
